title: Occupancy Verification and Property Preservation — CTL Policy
content:
Occupancy and Property Preservation Policy — Clear-To-List Requirements.

Purpose: Occupancy status directly impacts whether a property can be listed and under what conditions. Additionally, proper property preservation protects the asset value, ensures safety, and satisfies regulatory obligations. This policy establishes occupancy verification and property preservation standards for CTL determination.

Section 1 — Occupancy Status Categories:
Vacant-Secured: Property is unoccupied, all entry points are secured (locks changed, windows intact, doors locked), and the property is in a condition suitable for showing. CTL impact: Clear for listing, subject to other CTL criteria being met.
Vacant-Unsecured: Property is unoccupied but not properly secured (broken windows, open doors, evidence of unauthorized entry). CTL impact: ClearWithConditions — property must be secured before first showing. Listing may proceed but property must be secured within 5 business days.
Occupied-Authorized: Former borrower or authorized tenant is still in possession. CTL impact: Not clear for immediate listing as vacant possession. May be listed as occupied with appropriate disclosure if state law and investor guidelines permit occupied-property sales. Otherwise, eviction or voluntary vacancy must be completed first.
Occupied-Unauthorized: Squatter or unauthorized occupant is present. CTL impact: NeedsHumanReview — legal action required. Do not list until occupancy is resolved through law enforcement or legal proceedings.
Unknown: Occupancy has not been verified or the most recent inspection is stale (older than 30 days). CTL impact: NeedsHumanReview — field inspection must be ordered.

Section 2 — Field Inspection Currency:
Occupancy verification is considered current if the most recent field inspection was completed within 30 days of the CTL determination date. If more than 30 days have elapsed since the last inspection, a new inspection must be ordered. Inspections must include photographic evidence (exterior at minimum, interior preferred) and a signed occupancy certification by the inspector.

Section 3 — Eviction Proceedings:
When a property is occupied and the occupant must vacate before listing, lawful eviction proceedings must be followed per the applicable state's landlord-tenant or forcible entry and detainer statutes. Self-help eviction (e.g., changing locks on an occupied property, removing occupant belongings, shutting off utilities) is prohibited in all U.S. states and may expose the servicer and asset owner to significant legal liability. Expected eviction timelines vary by state: Non-judicial states with streamlined FED: 21 to 45 days. Judicial foreclosure states: 30 to 90 days. States with extended tenant protections (e.g., New York, California, New Jersey): 60 to 180 days or longer.

Section 4 — Cash-for-Keys Programs:
A Cash-for-Keys (C4K) agreement is a voluntary relocation incentive offered to the occupant as an alternative to formal eviction. If a C4K agreement has been executed with a defined move-out date, the property may be listed in advance with a showing restriction until the move-out date. The CTL verdict in this scenario is ClearWithConditions with the condition being confirmed vacancy on the agreed date. If the occupant does not vacate by the agreed date, the property must be re-evaluated and formal eviction proceedings initiated.

Section 5 — Property Preservation Standards:
Once a property is vacant, the following preservation requirements must be met: (a) Lock changes on all exterior doors — rekey to servicer or asset manager standard lock codes. (b) Winterization — in regions where temperatures drop below 35 degrees Fahrenheit, all plumbing must be winterized (water heater drained, supply lines blown out, antifreeze in traps). (c) Debris removal — all personal property left behind must be cataloged, stored per state abandoned property statutes (typically 15 to 30 days), then removed. (d) Yard maintenance — grass maintained below 10 inches, basic landscaping to prevent code violations. (e) Pool safety — if property has a pool, it must be secured with fencing or cover per local codes.

Section 6 — Hazardous Conditions:
If a property inspection reveals hazardous conditions (mold contamination, asbestos-containing materials, fire damage, structural instability, methamphetamine contamination), the CTL verdict is NeedsHumanReview. Remediation costs must be estimated before a listing decision. Properties with estimated remediation costs exceeding 25 percent of the as-is value should be evaluated for alternative disposition strategies (bulk sale, land bank donation, or demolition).

Section 7 — Reporting:
Every field inspection must produce a standardized report including: inspection date, inspector name and credentials, occupancy status finding, interior and exterior condition ratings (Good, Fair, Poor, Hazardous), photographic evidence, and any preservation work orders generated.

Section 8 — Pre-Verified Occupancy Exemption:
If the asset profile already records a confirmed Vacant occupancy status and the asset was ingested into the system within the last 7 days, occupancy verification is considered pre-satisfied for CTL determination purposes. In this scenario the Occupancy and Condition domain investigation may be omitted from the verification plan because the occupancy data is current and non-blocking. This exemption applies only to Tier 2 sellers. Tier 1 sellers require all conditions fully satisfied and must always undergo full occupancy investigation. Tier 3 sellers and any asset with Occupied or Unknown occupancy status must also always undergo full occupancy investigation regardless of ingestion recency.

References: HUD property preservation requirements as described in HUD Handbook 4000.1 and servicer participation agreements. State-specific eviction timelines based on applicable landlord-tenant statutes.
